messages:
raj.k: FYI ran a targeted stress run to compare INT8 vs FP8 for the KV cache under bursty small-batch workloads (RTX-pool, seq=512, temp=0.7). Results are funky — INT8 saves a lot of RAM but P95/P99 tail spikes show up during short concurrency surges.

emily: Can you paste the commands + a tiny profile snippet? Was this using kernel switching or a single kernel path?

raj.k: Command I used:
```bash
./perf_runner --model rdl-ggml-13b --kv-quant int8 --kernel auto --seq 512 --batcher bursty --concurrency 32 --runtime-opts "kv_cache=on,cache_quant_calib=epochal"
```
Profile snapshot (aggregated tokens/sec & latency):
```
CONFIG: KV=INT8, KERNEL=auto
median_tok_s: 1120
mean_lat_ms: 26.7
P95_lat_ms: 82.3  <-- noticeable jumps when bursts hit
P99_lat_ms: 185.6
mem_kb_per_shard: 420000  (40% less vs FP8)
```

ben: Interesting. With FP8 we saw smoother tail but higher steady-state memory, right? Numbers?

raj.k: Yes — FP8 steady-state P95 about 68ms, P99 140ms, mem 700k per shard. So FP8 wins latency, INT8 wins memory.

siva: Do we know if the auto kernel switcher is oscillating during bursts? That could explain tail spikes. Any kernel-switch logs?

raj.k: Perf-bot captured kernel-choice events:  spike pattern aligns with frequent kernel decisions when queue length oscillates 2->10->2. Kernel hysteresis TTL was 0s in this run.

perf-bot: kernel_switch: {from: fp8_conv, to: int8_avx, reason: mem_policy, time_ms: 158342, queue_len_before: 9} (repeated 47x over 120s)

emily: Ah — no hysteresis + aggressive auto-switch by mem_policy = churning. Suggest adding cooldown window or threshold on queue length delta before switching.

ben: Also want to rule out decode-quality regressions. Did you run log-prob drift evals on the outputs (sampling at temp 0.7)? INT8 sometimes distorts K/V enough to nudge topk, especially with prefix caching.

raj.k: Ran a quick BLEU-ish/QA-check across 200 prompt set: majority unchanged but 8% of prompts had token-level divergence after 120 tokens. Divergence correlated with early kernel switch events.

siva: So three interacting factors: quant noise (INT8), kernel switch churn, and batching hysteresis. Fix plan: 1) enable inter-switch cooldown (5s) 2) prefer latency-stable kernels during observed queue-jitter 3) conservative calibration mode for KV int8 (higher headroom)

emily: Agreed. Also propose a faster path: keep int8 for KV in memory-critical nodes but pin kernel at request-start if batcher predicts burst. We can detect bursty traffic via the moving stddev of queue length.

ben: For next run, can we increase batcher sampling window to 200ms and set kernel_hysteresis=5s? We'll compare: INT8+5s-hysteresis vs FP8 baseline.

raj.k: Scheduled: will run 4 experiments: FP8 baseline, INT8 no-hysteresis (repeat), INT8 hysteresis=5s, INT8 hysteresis=10s. Each run will be 15m with synthetic burst profile (80% idle, 20% 30rps bursts).

perf-bot: scheduled_job: perf.kv.burst.1945679000 -> runs in 5m

emily: Also dump kv-cache bit patterns for a few hot prompts (first 256 tokens) to see whether INT8 quantization creates systematic bias in high-attention heads. Binary diffs + per-head norms would help.

raj.k: Will add that. Quick sample diff output (head 2 norm):
```
FP8_head2_norm: 0.0123
INT8_head2_norm: 0.0091  (delta -26%)
```

siva: If certain heads lose magnitude consistently, we should add head-wise scale factors in post-calib to preserve decode distribution. Maybe calibrate with per-head scaling instead of global scale.

ben: Noted. Also keep an eye on tail latency source — whether it's kernel kernel-launch cost or memcpy amplification when switching layouts. Trace should include memcpy counts.

raj.k: Will collect trace + memcpy counters. For now, immediate mitigation: bump kernel_hysteresis to 5s and conservative int8-calib (clip to 4% extra head-scale). Will run and post results in this thread.

emily: Thanks — @perf-bot please tag when results land. :thumbsup: 

perf-bot: job_complete: perf.kv.burst.1945679000 status=complete (1945679130)

raj.k: First summary from INT8 + 5s-hysteresis: P95 improved from 82.3 -> 70.1ms, P99 185.6 -> 148.2ms, mem same ~420k. Divergence rate dropped from 8% -> 2%. Kernel_switch events reduced 47 -> 3.

ben: Nice. Does token throughput change?

raj.k: throughput steady ~1100 tok/s. FP8 baseline still slightly faster median but penalty in mem remains.

siva: Sounds like hysteresis + conservative calib gives best cost/quality trade. Next steps: bake hysteresis into kernel policy, add per-head post-calibration option behind feature flag, and run longer 24h stability test.

emily: I'll open an RFC for the policy changes and a checklist for the 24h run. Please include the mem vs latency SLAs so we can present tradeoffs to product.

raj.k: Filed RFC: https://rwd/ops/rfc/kv-quant-hysteresis-194567 (draft). Will post detailed traces here after 24h run.

ben: Thanks team. Small follow-ups: add unit test for kernel switch cooldown and add perf regression alert to catch P99 jumps >20% within 10m.

raj.k: On it. Closing loop after 24h.
